It updated the ADR README index, ran `just doc-check`, and made a signed local commit; nothing was pushed and the PR and #543 closure are still pending.

repo: ADRs in this repo are short: ADR 10 is the model, with a decision in two rules, two rejected options and a brief enforcement section that points at real code and tests.
Behaviour (resume, refuse, abort) belongs in `docs/specs/versioning.json`, not in ADRs.
Architecture placement (`GitAccess`, command layer, planning seam) belongs in `docs/architecture/versioning.md`, which already has an 'Idempotent apply' section.
ADR enforcement sections must name code and tests that exist, not planned ones.
`just doc-check` validates docs; the ADR README keeps an index that must be updated when adding an ADR.
Commits are signed (`git commit -S`) and verified via `git log --format='%h %G?'`.
The repo's own rule is to group trails by outcome; trails are not per-PR wrappers.
Auto-created trails can't be reparented through the CLI, so merged PRs stay in their existing trail.

code.finding: Rewritten to the decision-only shape: an interrupted `version` run records its inputs in a git ref and resumes from them.

workflow: Check existing artifacts (ADR 10, README conventions) before drafting a new one so it matches house style.
Don't reuse an open trail out of habit; check whether it matches the PR's outcome first.
Keep transient detail (bug-hunt narrative, timings, mechanics) out of durable docs like ADRs.
Don't stop for sign-off on every step when the direction is already agreed.
